findings.problem: Measured with GNU FriBidi 1.0.16 (--rtl) on the exact ur bytes: bare, the two commands paint 'approvals auto/' and 'new/' (the sigil lands on the RTL side, rule N2). src/i18n/bidi.ts isolateSigils (called by translate() for an RTL-answered message; the card renders through t() in approval-escape.tsx) fixes '/new' but wraps only '/approvals' (LATIN_WORD stops at the space), so '/approvals auto' paints as two LTR chunks in RTL order: 'auto /approvals' left-to-right (read right-to-left it is the correct order). Same behaviour as the shipped ur key ui.chat.pickers.mcp_command...'/mcp reauth'.
findings.fix: No wording change: the style guide forbids manual bidi controls and the string is byte-identical to core. If a one-chunk command is wanted, extend isolateSigils to take a following lowercase argument word (or isolate a multi-word command run) in src/i18n/bidi.ts; otherwise accept as the known seam limitation.
findings.disposition: not blocking; render seam, pre-existing, outside this PR's diff

findings.problem: The note writes the mode name as Latin 'auto' three times, while the sibling keys of the same namespace and card name the same mode in Urdu: mode.auto 'خودکار', set_session/set_all 'خودکار مقرر کریں', default_saved 'خودکار'. A reader who has just seen 'خودکار' on the same card sees 'auto' in the note that replaces those two links. Latin is defensible for the argument of the typed command '/approvals auto' and it matches core wire.bridge_taint.* (kept so for byte-identity), but the two prose uses 'auto بند ہیں' and 'auto آن کرنے' could read 'خودکار'.
findings.fix: Optional: in prose use 'خودکار' and keep Latin 'auto' only inside the command; that breaks byte-identity with core, so it would need the core file changed in step. Recorded, not required.
findings.disposition: not blocking; inherited from core text
